children: Chinese regulators on Monday introduced stricter rules governing automakers' payments to suppliers, seeking to close loopholes in the industry's voluntary 60-day payment commitment, including delays in product acceptance procedures and the use of non-cash payment instruments.

As authorities moved to curb the industry's bruising price war, major Chinese automakers last year pledged to pay suppliers within 60 days, following complaints from steel producers and other suppliers about lengthy payment cycles.
